body_md:
Let $Q$ denote Cappell--Shaneson's exotic $\mathbb{RP}^4$. This is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{RP}^4$ but not stably diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{RP}^4$, i.e. there does not exist a $k$ such that $\mathbb{RP}^4\#k(S^2\times S^2)$ and $Q\#k(S^2\times S^2)$ are diffeomorphic \cite[p.61]{Cappell-Shaneson}. See \cite[Section~5.6.]{counterexamples} for a discussion of properties of $Q$ and further examples of exotic $\mathbb{RP}^4$s. There is a diffeomorphism $f\colon Q\#\mathbb{CP}^2\to \mathbb{RP}^4\#\mathbb{CP}^2$ by \cite[Theorem~2]{akbulut}, see also \cite[Theorem~18]{bais-torres}. Let $s_0\colon S^2\to \mathbb{RP}^4\#\mathbb{CP}^2$ be the embedding of $\mathbb{CP}^1$ into $\mathbb{CP}^2$. Similarly, let $s_1'\colon S^2\to Q\#\mathbb{CP}^2$ be the embedding of $\mathbb{CP}^1$ into $\mathbb{CP}^2$ and define $s_1:=f\circ s_1'$. By definition the exteriors of $s_0$ and $s_1$ are diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{RP}^4\setminus \mathring{D}^4$ and $Q\setminus \mathring{D}^4$, respectively. In particular, since the exteriors are homeomorphic, the embeddings are topologically equivalent but not externally stably smoothly equivalent. This example of exotic embedded spheres is \cite[Example~19]{bais-torres}.
		
		To complete the proof of (1) it remains to show that the embeddings $s_0$ and $s_1$ do not become externally stably diffeomorphic after any number of internal stabilisations.
		Let $s^g\colon \Sigma_g\to \mathbb{CP}^2$ be the internal, $g$-fold stabilisation of $\mathbb{CP}^1\to \mathbb{CP}^2$. Since the embedding is characteristic, the exterior $\mathbb{CP}^2_{s^g}$ is spin. Since $\mathbb{CP}^2_{s^g}\times I$ is a nullbordism of its boundary, $\mathbb{CP}^2_{s^g}\cup_\partial\mathbb{CP}^2_{s^g}\cong\partial(\mathbb{CP}^2_{s^g}\times I)$ has trivial signature. By Novikov additivity, it follows that gluing two copies of $\mathbb{CP}^2_{s^g}$ along any diffeomorphism of their boundaries has trivial signature. 
		
		Let $s_i^g$ be the internal, $g$-fold stabilisation of $s_i$. Their complements are diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{RP}^4\#\mathbb{CP}^2_{s^g}$ and $Q\#\mathbb{CP}^2_{s^g}$, respectively. In particular they admit a pin$^+$-structure. Any pin$^+$-structure will induce the unique spin-structure on $\mathbb{CP}^2_{s^g}$ and thus a unique spin structure on the boundary. Assume there is a stably diffeomorphism $h\colon \mathbb{RP}^4\#\mathbb{CP}^2_{s^g}\#k(S^2\times S^2)\to Q\#\mathbb{CP}^2_{s^g}\#k(S^2\times S^2)$. We pick pin$^+$-structures such that $h$ is pin$^+$-structure preserving. In particular, it preserves the induced spin structure on the boundary. Gluing along the boundary with $\mathbb{CP}^2_{s^g}$, we to obtain a diffeomorphism between the closed manifolds $\mathbb{RP}^4\#X_1\#k(S^2\times S^2)$ and $Q\#X_2\#k(S^2\times S^2)$, where $X_i$ is a spin manifold consisting of two copies of $\mathbb{CP}^2_{s^g}$ glued along the boundary. As discussed in the previous paragraph, $X_i$ has trivial signature. Since $X_i$ is also simply-connected, it is stably diffeomorphic to $l$ copies of $S^2\times S^2$ for some $l$. It follows that $RP^4$ and $Q$ are stably diffeomorphic, a contradiction. Hence $s_0$ and $s_1$ are internally and externally stably exotic as claimed.

title: Proof
body_md:
An application of Kreck's modified surgery yields that, for $n$ large enough, the manifolds~$X:=(S^2\times \mathbb{RP}^2)\#(n+11)(S^2\times S^2)$ and $X':=(S^2\times \mathbb{RP}^2)\#K3\#n(S^2\times S^2)$ are diffeomorphic, see also \cite[Theorem~A]{KP-stablyexotic}. Let $f\colon X'\to X$ be such a diffeomorphism. Let $s_0\colon S^2\to (S^2\times \mathbb{RP}^2)\#(n+11)(S^2\times S^2)$ be given by taking $S^2\times\{*\}$ in $S^2\times \mathbb{RP}^2$. Similarly, let $s_1'\colon S^2\to (S^2\times \mathbb{RP}^2)\#K3\#n(S^2\times S^2)$  be given by taking $S^2\times\{*\}$ in $S^2\times \mathbb{RP}^2$. We set $s_1:=f\circ s_1'$. Let $M$ be the M\"obius band. Then the complement of $\nu s_0$ is diffeomorphic to $(S^2\times M)\# (n+11)(S^2\times S^2)$ while the complement of $\nu s_1$ is diffeomorphic to $(S^2\times M)\#K3\#n(S^2\times S^2)$. Let $s_0^g$ and $s_1^g$ denote the $g$-fold internal stabilisations of $s_0$ and $s_1$. The boundary of $\nu s^g_i$ is diffeomorphic to $S^1\times \Sigma_g$ for $i=0,1$. Let $W_g$ and $W_g'$ denote the complements of $\nu s_0^g$ and $\nu s_1^g$, respectively.
		
		Assume there is a diffeomorphism taking $s_0^g$ to $s_1^g$ after taking a $k$-fold external stabilisation. Then this diffeomorphism induces a bundle isomorphism on the normal bundles and thus gives a diffeomorphism $h$ from $W_g\#k(S^2\times S^2)$ to $W_g'\#k(S^2\times S^2)$ that respects the structure of an $S^1$ bundle on the boundary. All bundle automorphism of the trivial $S^1$-bundle $S^1\times \Sigma_g$ extend over $M\times \Sigma_g$ and we obtain well-defined manifolds $X_g:=W_g\cup_\partial(M\times \Sigma_g)\#k(S^2\times S^2)$ and $X'_g:=W'_g\cup_\partial(M\times \Sigma_g)\#k(S^2\times S^2)$, where we choose the gluing map for $X'_g$ by postcomposing the gluing map for $X_g$ with $h\mid_{\partial W_g}$.  Hence we also obtain a diffeomorphism $h\cup\operatorname{id}\colon X_g\to X'_g$.
		 
		We now seek alternate descriptions of $X_g$ and $X'_g$ that are more amenable to the methods of modified surgery (as in \cite{KP-stablyexotic}).  Performing the internal stabilisations of $S^2\times\{*\}$ inside $S^2\times \mathbb{RP}^2$ yields a surface whose exterior $C$ is a manifold with fundamental group $\mathbb{Z}$ and boundary $S^1\times \Sigma_g$. Let $Y_g:=C\cup_\partial M\times \Sigma_g$. The inclusion of the boundary induces maps \[\pi_1(S^1\times \Sigma_g)\to \pi_1(S^1)\cong \mathbb{Z}\xrightarrow{\cdot 2}\mathbb{Z}\cong \pi_1(C)\] and \[\pi_1(S^1\times \Sigma_g)\cong \mathbb{Z}\oplus\pi_1(\Sigma_g)\xrightarrow{(\cdot 2,1)}\mathbb{Z}\oplus\pi_1(\Sigma_g)\cong \pi_1(M\times \Sigma_g).\]
		By Seifert--van Kampen it follows that $\pi_1(Y_g)$ is isomorphic to the pushout of $\mathbb{Z}\xleftarrow{\cdot 2}\mathbb{Z}\xrightarrow{\cdot 2}\mathbb{Z}$ which is the fundamental group of the Klein bottle. In particular, $\pi_1(Y_g)$ is 2-dimensional.
		
		By construction $X_g$ is diffeomorphic to $Y_g\#(n+k+11)(S^2\times S^2)$, while $X'_g$ is diffeomorphic to $Y_g\#K3\#(n+k)(S^2\times S^2)$. It follows again from Kreck's modified surgery theory, e.g.\ an application of \cite[Theorem~A, (iii)]{KP-stablyexotic} (using that $\pi_1(Y_g)$ is 2-dimensional), that $X_g$ and $X'_g$ are not stably diffeomorphic. This contradicts the existence of $h$. Hence $s_0^g$ and $s_1^g$ are not externally stably diffeomorphic.
